Build a gtsummary table from a SAS %summarytable-style grouped variable list

Source: R/hv-tbl-summary.R
hv_tbl_summary.Rd

Thin wrapper over gtsummary::tbl_summary() modeled on the interface biostats team members already know from the %summarytable SAS macro: a grouped, ordered variable list (groups, the macro's LIST= equivalent) and variable-type buckets (continuous/binary/ categorical, the CON3=/CAT1=/CAT2= equivalents), rather than gtsummary's own tidyselect-based interface. Returns a plain gtsummary object, ready for hv_man_table().

Usage

hv_tbl_summary(
  data,
  by = NULL,
  groups,
  continuous = character(0),
  binary = character(0),
  categorical = character(0),
  compare = c("pvalue", "smd", "both", "none"),
  percentiles = c(15, 85),
  overall = TRUE,
  continuous_stat = c("median", "mean", "both"),
  normal = character(0),
  mean_sd = character(0),
  show_variable = TRUE,
  cutexact = "any",
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

by

Grouping variable name as a string (%summarytable CLASS= equivalent), or NULL for a single ungrouped "Overall" column.

groups

Named list, section label -> variable names in display order (%summarytable LIST= equivalent), e.g. list(Demography = c("age", "female"), Symptoms = c("nyha")). Each section must name at least one variable; a section holding character(0) is an error, not an empty section. Every variable named here must appear in exactly one of continuous, binary, or categorical, and every classified variable must appear in groups.

continuous

Character vector of continuous variable names (%summarytable CON3= equivalent), summarized as set by continuous_stat. Variables the macro classified as CON1= (mean +/- SD, one-way ANOVA) or CON2= (median with min and max) belong here too; list CON1= variables in normal as well to keep the macro's mean +/- SD and ANOVA. Each named column must be numeric.

binary

Character vector of 0/1 variable names (%summarytable CAT1= equivalent), summarized as n (%) on a single row. Each named column must have at most 2 distinct non-NA values, and must be logical, 0/1, or Yes/No data, so that the "event" the single row counts is unambiguous. Anything else belongs in categorical, which shows every level. The event is the TRUE, 1, or Yes side, and is stated to gtsummary explicitly rather than inferred, so columns read from SAS with haven::read_sas() summarize the same as their plain-vector equivalents.

categorical

Character vector of multi-level variable names (%summarytable CAT2= equivalent), summarized as n (%) per level. No type rule applies: factors, characters, and small-integer codes are all accepted. Ordinal variables belong here too; this function does not run a trend test (%summarytable's ORD1= distinction is not preserved).

compare

One of "pvalue" (default), "smd", "both", or "none". Ignored (treated as "none") when by is NULL, since there is nothing to compare. "smd" and "both" require by to have exactly two groups, because a standardized mean difference is defined between two of them; they error otherwise. "pvalue" and "none" work at any number of groups. %summarytable PVALUES= equivalent, and ASD= only in part: the "smd" number is gtsummary's generic standardized mean difference (gtsummary::add_difference()), a proportion computed alike for every continuous variable. %summarytable's column came from the %stddiff macro, which treats non-Gaussian and ordinal variables differently and prints a percentage, so the two disagree for those variables (by 30% on one skewed test variable). To show %stddiff's number, compute it with hvtiRpropensity::ps_stddiff() and add it with hv_tbl_compare(), beside compare = "pvalue" if wanted.

percentiles

Numeric vector of length 2, the low/high percentile pair for continuous summaries, as increasing whole numbers between 0 and 100. Default c(15, 85), the hv_man_footnotes() house convention (%summarytable PP= equivalent).

overall

Single TRUE/FALSE. When TRUE (default), prepends an Overall column across all groups (%summarytable TOTALCOL=1, the macro's default). Ignored when by is NULL, since the single column already is the overall one.

continuous_stat

One of "median" (default), "mean", or "both": how continuous variables not listed in normal are summarized. "median" gives median [P<low>, P<high>]; "mean" gives mean +/- SD, with no spaces around the plus-minus sign and EHB/Blackstone paired rounding; "both" puts the two side by side: each group's statistic column shows mean +/- SD (or n (%) for a categorical row), and a median column beside it shows median [P<low>, P<high>], blank on rows with no median. Both renderers lay it out the same way. Choosing one for the manuscript is then a matter of dropping a column. The test does not change with the statistic: only normal selects ANOVA. The CORR footnote carried through hv_man_table() to hv_man_table_save() follows this choice automatically. Placed after overall so calls passing overall by position keep working.

normal

Character vector, a subset of continuous: the variables to treat as normally distributed (%summarytable CON1= equivalent). Each is summarized as mean +/- SD whatever continuous_stat says, and, under compare = "pvalue" or "both", tested with classical (pooled-variance) one-way ANOVA, the test the macro ran. Default none. Each name must also appear in continuous. Placed after continuous_stat so positional calls keep working. To show mean +/- SD without the ANOVA, use mean_sd.

mean_sd

Character vector, a subset of continuous: the variables to display as mean +/- SD while keeping the nonparametric test (Wilcoxon rank-sum, or Kruskal-Wallis for 3+ groups). Use it for variables that are roughly symmetric in a table whose every continuous test should stay nonparametric. The display is the same as for normal, cell mark included when the table mixes statistics; only normal changes the test. A variable may appear in both, and is then tested with ANOVA. Default none. Last in the signature so positional calls keep working.

show_variable

Single TRUE/FALSE. When TRUE (default), adds a "Variable" column beside the label holding each variable's column name in data, on its first row, as %summarytable's report did. It belongs to the report view: hv_man_table() and hv_man_table_display() show it, while hv_man_table_save() always drops it and the manuscript style never shows it, so a saved table is a manuscript table whatever this says. Set FALSE to leave it out of the report view too.

cutexact

When a binary or categorical variable is tested with Fisher's exact test rather than Pearson's chi-square (no continuity correction). The default, "any", uses Fisher whenever any one group-by-level cell has an expected count below 5 (gtsummary's rule, and what the CORR team asked for). A number opts in to %summarytable's CUTEXACT= rule, to reproduce a SAS table: Fisher when at least that percentage of cells expect fewer than 5. The macro's default was 50; 0 makes every categorical test exact and a value above 100 makes none exact. In the CORR table each Fisher p-value is marked with a superscript double dagger, footnoted "Fisher exact test.", in every style. Used only when compare produces p-values. The other tests that ran are named in the dagger note instead, as "P values from the Wilcoxon rank sum test and Pearson's chi-square test.", and the CORR table puts the dagger on the p-value header too. compare = "smd" or "both" names the difference column "Std. Diff." and the same note says what it is.

...

Not used. Present so that %summarytable parameter names produce an error naming the argument to use instead.

Value

A gtsummary object, ready for hv_man_table(). See Details for the hv_stat_label, hv_trailing, and hv_footnotes renderer attributes. A table whose rows mix mean and median also carries hv_cell_marks, a list with symbol ("§" or "¶") and variables (the names whose cells carry it); the attribute is NULL otherwise. The manuscript style also reads hv_by_label, the grouping's name (the variable's label when the data carry one), and the hidden hv_n column of table_body, each variable's overall non-missing count.

Details

Continuous variables are summarized as median [P<low>, P<high>] by default, or as mean +/- SD, or both (continuous_stat), and tested non-parametrically (Wilcoxon rank-sum for 2 groups, Kruskal-Wallis for 3+), the macro's CON3=. A variable you also list in normal is the macro's CON1= instead: mean +/- SD, tested with one-way ANOVA. percentiles defaults to the house convention documented in hv_man_footnotes() (15th/85th), overridable per study (%summarytable equivalent: PP=).

The house notation: each median and percentile is shown to 2 significant digits, and a value of 10 or more to the units place (102 [63, 170], 0.31 [0.21, 0.39]), and a P value has no leading zero (.013, <.001, >.9).

When rows of one table show different statistics, the header and dagger name the statistic most rows use, and the cells of the other are marked instead of the row labels (the macro's DESCLABEL=1 suffixes, such as "Age, Mean±SD", are gone). When more rows show mean +/- SD than a median, the mean is the default and a section sign (§) marks the median cells; otherwise a pilcrow (¶) marks the mean cells. Each mark has its own footnote. A tie leaves the median as the default.

Mean/SD output follows Eugene H. Blackstone's (EHB's) paired reporting rule: the mean is rounded to the first-significant-digit place of the SD, and the SD is rounded one place finer. When the SD begins with 1, both retain one additional place. Exact ties round to even; values beyond a tie round up. This applies to every group and Overall column when continuous_stat = "mean", and to the mean row under "both". Medians and percentiles follow the house notation above instead, and their exact ties also round to even, as for mean +/- SD: 62.5 shows as 62, where gtsummary and SAS showed 63. When an SD is zero or unavailable, no paired precision can be inferred, so gtsummary's existing display is kept.

The returned object carries these renderer attributes: hv_stat_label, the sub-header text naming the statistics shown ("No. (%) or Median [<low>, <high> percentiles]" by default, with ordinal suffixes; it follows continuous_stat); hv_trailing, a named character vector ready to pass as naming the comparison columns the manuscript style shows, when compare produced one (NULL when compare = "none"); and hv_footnotes, the CORR footnote block that hv_man_table() carries into hv_man_table_save() so the default dagger follows continuous_stat and percentiles automatically. A mixed table also carries hv_cell_marks, the symbol and variables whose cells hv_man_table() marks, and a table built with continuous_stat = "both" carries hv_median_label.

Common mistakes

"<var> appears in more than one of continuous, binary, and categorical." Each variable is classified exactly once. A 0/1 variable is binary; a multi-level factor is categorical.

"continuous lists <var>, but <var> is factor data ..." The bucket has to suit the data, not just be free of overlaps. A non-numeric variable in continuous used to reach gtsummary, which only messages about it, and produced a complete, correctly styled table whose every statistic was NA.

"binary lists <var>, but <var> has ..." binary renders one n (%) row, so it takes at most two distinct values and needs an unambiguous event value: logical, 0/1, or Yes/No. A three-level factor, or a two-level one like F/M, belongs in categorical.

"Variable(s) in groups not classified ..." Every variable listed in groups also needs a type bucket, and every classified variable needs to appear in groups. The two lists must match.

"compare = "smd" requires exactly two groups." A standardized mean difference is defined between two groups. Use compare = "pvalue" for three or more. If by is a factor with an unused level, droplevels() is usually what you want.

"by must not also be listed in groups." by is the grouping variable being compared across, not a row to summarize. Before this check existed, the combination reached gtsummary and failed several calls later with "names must be NULL or a character vector, not an empty integer vector.", a message that never mentioned by. Remove the variable from groups.

See also

hv_man_table() to render the result. hv_man_footnotes() for the percentile-footnote house convention.

Examples

# A baseline-characteristics table of the kind a study manuscript
# actually carries: demography and disease sections, compared
# across treatment arms.
hv_tbl_summary(
  gtsummary::trial,
  by = "trt",
  groups = list(
    Demography = c("age", "marker"),
    Disease = c("stage", "grade")
  ),
  continuous = c("age", "marker"),
  categorical = c("stage", "grade")
)
